learning_outcomes.text: Address the complete implementation of an “embedded system” based on microprocessors and/or microcontrollers in their professional life.
Fluently handle the datasheets of typical electronic components of embedded systems: microprocessors, microcontrollers and peripheral integrated circuits.
Connect various devices (memories, I/O controllers, etc.) with a microprocessor and/or microcontroller based on their needs and given specifications.

Understand the characteristics of microcontrollers, establish their field of application and select the most suitable microcontroller for a given application, from technical and economic points of view.
Know the programming language for a given microprocessor/microcontroller, and handle the most common development tools: assembler, compilers, simulators, emulators, etc., that facilitate development.
Work in a group, reason critically to compare different solutions and discriminate the most optimal one.
Acquire the ability to solve open problems and projects through analysis and information search. Defend their solution against other possibilities through oral communication.
Use A/D and D/A conversion circuits, both discrete and integrated into microcontrollers or other devices.
Design and implement digital systems using timer blocks, A/D and D/A converters integrated into microcontrollers, and select the optimal one for each application.
Know and use the most common digital communication buses and standards between systems (RS-232, RS-485, etc.) and between integrated circuits (SPI, I2C, etc.).
Manage and design complex I/O circuits and interfaces, such as LCDs and their associated circuits, both at a logical and electrical level.

Use programmable logic devices as one more component within electronic design, distinguishing when their use is advantageous compared to other alternatives and handling their various debugging and development tools for a given family.

syllabus_topics: Operation of a minimum microprocessor system
Internal organization and Exceptions of the 68000
teaching_methods: Classroom practice sessions for problem solving
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in both the Laboratory block (30% of final grade) and the Theory block (70% of final grade) to pass the course. If both minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.3*LAB + 0.7*THEORY, with a minimum overall final score of 5. If either block score is below 4, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 or the weighted sum of both blocks. For extraordinary calls, if a laboratory block score above 4 was obtained in the ordinary call, it can be maintained, otherwise a personal work or exam will be assigned; the theory block combines partial exams (30%) and a final exam (70%) of the block. The same minimums and weighted average apply.
